mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has moved inversely to RETAIL_REC across all four observed weeks (e.g., RESIDENTIAL peaked at 13.1 when RETAIL_REC troughed at -12.0). This stable inverse coupling reflects a fixed activity budget: time spent at home substitutes directly for out-of-home retail trips. As RESIDENTIAL mean-reverts toward its 4-week average, RETAIL_REC should correspondingly recover upward over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise (or falls further) over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL declining from its current elevated level of ~10-13 points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has held in a narrow elevated band (6.3-7.1) for the last three weeks, indicating essential-shopping demand has already saturated at a new baseline. Once essential trips plateau, households have limited residual capacity to add discretionary retail trips, capping near-term growth in RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above +5 for 3 or more consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises by more than 2 points over the next 2 weeks even though GROCERY_PHARM stays above +5 throughout that period.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES dropped sharply to -16.1 at t-1w then rebounded to -6.6 at t-0w, a pattern consistent with a short-lived restriction being lifted. Such rapid policy reversals historically precede a broader reopening wave that increases foot traffic to retail and recreation venues over the following month as confidence in stability builds.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES stabilizing above -8 for at least two consecutive weeks following the rebound.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES move together as commuting-linked series; when both rise concurrently (less negative), it signals restored commuting routines that generate incidental retail stops on the way to/from work, lifting RETAIL_REC. Neither series alone is as predictive as their joint co-movement.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increase (become less negative) in the same week relative to the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 2 weeks in a week where both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rose together relative to the prior week.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS has declined in the most recent week to -16.7, its lowest point in the snapshot, suggesting a seasonal or weather-driven shift away from outdoor activity. This outdoor-to-indoor substitution effect should redirect some leisure time toward indoor retail and recreation venues within the coming week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following a week where PARKS fell below -15.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has stayed persistently depressed (-17.4 to -20.4) across all four weeks, indicating sustained public-transit avoidance behavior. Because many retail destinations in dense commercial corridors depend on transit access, continued suppression of transit use will constrain RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -15 for 4 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises by more than 2 points over the next 2 weeks while TRANSIT remains below -15 throughout.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL (around +10 to +13) combined with saturated GROCERY_PHARM demand (+6 to +7) together indicate households are maximizing time at home while already meeting essential needs, leaving little behavioral room for discretionary retail expansion. The joint persistence of both conditions is a stronger suppressor than either series alone.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +10 and GROCERY_PHARM stays above +5 simultaneously for 3+ weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite both RESIDENTIAL remaining above +10 and GROCERY_PHARM remaining above +5 throughout that period.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in PARKS (to -16.7) alongside a rise in RESIDENTIAL (to 10.6+) in the most recent week signals a tightening-restriction regime where outdoor and discretionary movement are both curtailed together, typically preceding reduced retail footfall as restrictions bite over the following month.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises while PARKS falls in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite PARKS and RESIDENTIAL moving in this tightening pattern (PARKS down, RESIDENTIAL up) in the final observed week.
